**My reasoning as this farmer:**

I've been working this land my whole life. My father did it, his father did it. In Quzhou, we grow wheat in winter and maize in summer — that's just what you do here on the North China Plain. The soil knows these crops. I know these crops. Buyers are always there for both. Why would I change?

I have about 10 mu. My wife helps during busy periods but our children are in the city now, so I keep it manageable. I can't afford to experiment — at 60, a bad harvest is a serious problem.

For wheat, I'll do rotary tillage in October before planting. I'll use improved certified seed from the county agri-supply station — they've been reliable and yields are better than old varieties. I'll apply base fertilizer before sowing, then top-dress nitrogen at jointing. I water four times: before sowing, wintering water in November, jointing in April, and heading in May. The groundwater is getting harder to pump every year but I still do it. I'll spray herbicide in late autumn and fungicide once in spring.

After wheat harvest in June I go straight into maize — no time to till, I just direct seed into the stubble. Hybrid seed,郑单958 or whatever the local station has. Maize only needs one or two waterings since the rains come in July and August. I'll side-dress urea around the V6 stage.
